A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A.1–A.5. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support a reliable comparison of all scientific content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, computational efficiency measurements and error analyses in Section 4, Table 1 and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results, including model performance, computational efficiency and template-adherence analyses.

M1.justification: The T5 and BERT2BERT architectures, GPT-4-generated supervision, reporting template and training/adaptation procedures are identical in Section 3 and Appendices A.1–A.4.

E1.justification: Both use MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert Plus for the same chest-radiology report structuring task. Training coverage, evaluated populations and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same five LLMs participate in the adaptation comparison, and the same LLaMA-3 sizes participate in the scaling benchmark. Comparator membership and adaptation variants in Tables 5–7 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Data splits, report parsing, evaluation metrics, model sizes and training budgets are identical. This includes the single-epoch LLaMA-3-70B configuration and the settings in Appendices A.3–A.4.

E4.justification: The pretraining-domain comparisons, adaptation and scaling analyses, qualitative example, and template-adherence error analysis are unchanged, including Section 4.4 and Table 8.

E5.justification: Both report three training runs with different random seeds for the lightweight configurations and 95% confidence intervals in Figure 3. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1 and 4–8, plotted results in Figures 3–5, and qualitative findings are identical. No result entries, rankings or reported trends change.

T1.justification: Mathematical content and metric descriptions are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight models' competitive performance and computational advantages over adapted LLMs.

C2.justification: The discussion and all eight limitations are identical, including qualifications about GPT-4 supervision, population coverage, ICL selection bias and limited LLM finetuning.

D1.justification: Prompt details, checkpoint descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware information and resource-access links are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement supplies no new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, research positioning and cited works are identical. References move within pages 9–12 because of the acknowledgement insertion; none are added or removed.

P1.justification: V2 adds a short Acknowledgements section between Limitations and References, crediting MIDRC/NIBIB/NIH and ARPA-H support. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts the references across pages 9–12, and the first-page version stamp changes. Figures, tables and the entire appendix retain identical rendered layouts.

improvement.justification: V2 makes funding attribution more complete through the new acknowledgement, but leaves the scientific evidence, reproducibility details, interpretations and appendices unchanged. This administrative addition and the accompanying reference reflow do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
